sources.entry: SimpleLocalize CLI - Open source tool for managing i18n keys in software projects.

summary.one_liner: SimpleLocalize CLI is a command-line tool for managing translation files in software projects, aimed at CI/CD pipelines and localization automation.
summary.what_it_does: The CLI uploads local translation files to SimpleLocalize and downloads translations back to local files in a chosen format and language set. It can start auto-translation tasks for project languages and wait for them to finish. It also publishes and pulls translations to and from translation hosting environments. Other commands include status (print project details), purge (remove all translations, keys and languages), init (create a sample config file), and extract (find translation keys in source code by search directory and project type). Settings can come from a simplelocalize.yml file, command-line flags, or the SIMPLELOCALIZE_API_KEY environment variable, with flags overriding the config file. A language mapping option controls how the {lang} placeholder maps to file paths, and HTTP/HTTPS proxies are supported.
use_cases: sync translation files with a web or mobile app project
download translations in multiple languages into project files
extract translation keys from source code
how_to_run: macOS / Linux / Windows (WSL): curl -s | bash (installer script, URL not shown in README)
simplelocalize init (creates a sample configuration file)
simplelocalize upload --apiKey PROJECT_API_KEY --uploadPath INPUT_FILE --uploadFormat FILE_FORMAT --uploadLanguageKey en
simplelocalize download --apiKey PROJECT_API_KEY --downloadPath DOWNLOAD_PATH --downloadFormat FILE_FORMAT --downloadLanguageKey en,de,fr
notable: Config file (simplelocalize.yml) with language mapping for {lang} placeholders, e.g. writing English to values/ instead of values-en/
Auto-translate command waits for translation tasks to finish
Binary installer for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Linux (x86 and ARM64), and Windows
Extract command scans source code for translation keys
caveats: Every command requires a project API key
Detailed documentation lives in the GitHub Wiki rather than the README
README does not state a license beyond pointing to a LICENSE file
